title: Cloudflare Launches Persistent, Stateful, Computer-like Environments for Agents
gist: Cloudflare has open-sourced Cloudflare Computer, an agent runtime that gives each AI agent a persistent, stateful 'computer' built on isolates rather than a dedicated container, with the platform deciding whether work runs in an isolate, a container sandbox or a browser. The explicit premise is that container-per-agent cannot scale to billions of concurrent agents because the global compute capacity does not exist; the target is under 10% of agent work needing a container, with a shared SQLite-backed filesystem bridging isolates and containers. It is an early preview suitable only for prototypes.

insights.claim: Cloudflare argues that running AI agents in containers will not scale to hundreds of millions and then billions of concurrent agents because there is simply not enough global compute capacity for that model.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: If agent concurrency is capacity-bound, the winners are runtimes with the lowest per-agent overhead, not the ones with the most GPU or container fleet.
insights.quote: hundreds of millions, then billions, of concurrent agents
insights.locator: Cloudflare Computer attempts to tackle a major challenge

insights.claim: Cloudflare's stated design target is a runtime in which a container is required for less than 10% of an agent's work, with coding tasks, audio/video manipulation and document creation all handled inside isolates.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A 10x-plus reduction in container-hours per agent would reset the unit economics of agent hosting and pressure container-based agent-sandbox vendors.
insights.quote: Our goal with @cloudflare/computer is to provide an agent with a runtime where a container is required for less than 10% of its work, and coding tasks, audio/video manipulation, and document creation can all be handled by isolates.
insights.locator: To address this, the @cloudflare/computer package introduces an agent runtime

insights.claim: Cloudflare frames isolates, originally introduced with Cloudflare Workers, as infinitely horizontally scalable with extremely fast startup and shutdown, which is the basis of its cost claim for agent workloads.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Cloudflare is reusing an existing serverless primitive rather than building new infrastructure, so incremental capex to serve agents is low relative to container-based rivals.
insights.locator: According to Cloudflare, isolates, which were introduced with Cloudflare Workers

insights.claim: In Cloudflare Computer the platform, not the developer, decides whether code runs in an isolate, a container sandbox or a web browser, so each agent gets a computer while the runtime optimizes for efficiency and scalability.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Placement as a platform decision is the abstraction that lets a vendor arbitrage cheap and expensive compute — and locks customers into that vendor's scheduler.
insights.quote: each agent gets a computer, the runtime optimizes for efficiency, and scalability
insights.locator: To address this, the @cloudflare/computer package introduces an agent runtime

insights.claim: The architecture runs the agent harness inside an isolate hosted in a Durable Object and calls an attached container on-demand as a tool, using heavier compute primitives only when required.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Container-as-a-tool rather than container-as-a-host is the concrete pattern to evaluate when costing any agent platform.
insights.quote: Cloudflare’s architecture has been designed to run the agent harness in the isolate (in a Durable Object) and call an attached container on-demand as a tool.
insights.locator: Cloudflare maintains that this combination of isolates and container sandboxes

insights.claim: Cloudflare's efficiency claim rests on combining horizontal scalability from isolates with vertical scalability from container sandboxes rather than choosing between them.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A hybrid scaling story is hard for pure-container agent platforms to match without rebuilding their execution layer.
insights.locator: Cloudflare maintains that this combination of isolates and container sandboxes

insights.claim: Isolates in this runtime persist agent state and hibernate when the agent is not running, and can spin up their own container sandboxes on demand — giving agents durable, computer-like environments instead of ephemeral ones.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Hibernating persistent state means idle agents cost near-nothing, which is what makes long-lived per-user agents economically viable.
insights.locator: Additionally, they can persist the agent state, hibernate

insights.claim: A shared SQLite-based filesystem accessible to both isolates and containers is the central architectural piece, letting tasks move seamlessly between the two while working on the same files.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: The shared filesystem is the load-bearing dependency: if it is slow or lossy, the whole isolate/container hybrid collapses back into container-per-agent.
insights.locator: One central piece in this architecture is a shared, SQLite-based filesystem

insights.claim: Cloudflare Computer filesystems can be backed by git repositories, storage buckets or arbitrary files while ensuring all operations are gated, audited and observed.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Built-in gating and audit of agent file operations is the governance hook enterprises will demand before letting agents touch code repositories.
insights.locator: Cloudflare Computer filesystems can be used with git repositories

insights.claim: Cloudflare Computer currently ships three backends: container projects exposing SQLite state as a real FUSE-mounted filesystem inside a sandboxed container, isolate shells running a just-bash environment in a Dynamic Worker, and isolate JavaScript running an ECMAScript module in a fresh Dynamic Worker.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Bash-in-an-isolate is the key capability to test — it determines whether typical coding-agent workloads really escape containers.
insights.locator: Currently, Cloudflare Computer provides three backends

insights.claim: Cloudflare itself says Cloudflare Computer is an early preview only suitable for experiments, exploration and prototypes, so the scaling claims are unproven in production.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Discount the billions-of-agents narrative for now; the announcement is a positioning move on the agent-runtime standard, not shipped capacity.
insights.locator: Cloudflare Computer is still an early preview

insights.claim: Cloudflare released the agent runtime as open source rather than a proprietary service, a distribution choice aimed at making its isolate model the default substrate for agent execution.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Open-sourcing the runtime while keeping the isolate platform proprietary is the classic funnel play — watch adoption of @cloudflare/computer as the leading indicator.
